### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**23** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ea3fe9eaa8cf43657cb66b119f6ed15ac43d19c`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ea3fe9eaa8cf43657cb66b119f6ed15ac43d19c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `01077f7b01557c975c39a842a5a837886b725914` — the merge of head `295ae9d8c8bac731f9b8a99f3192070fcd1e13af` into base `1ea3fe9eaa8cf43657cb66b119f6ed15ac43d19c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 01077f7b01557c975c39a842a5a837886b725914 && git checkout 01077f7b01557c975c39a842a5a837886b725914
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ea3fe9eaa8cf43657cb66b119f6ed15ac43d19c 295ae9d8c8bac731f9b8a99f3192070fcd1e13af && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ea3fe9eaa8cf43657cb66b119f6ed15ac43d19c && git merge --no-ff 295ae9d8c8bac731f9b8a99f3192070fcd1e13af

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ea3fe9eaa8cf43657cb66b119f6ed15ac43d19c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1ea3fe9eaa8cf43657cb66b119f6ed15ac43d19c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `@objectstack/service-automation` gains three public exports on its barrel (`index.ts` L148-155): `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIALS_UI_BUNDLE` (a manifest-shaped plugin bundle: `id com.objectstack.service-automation.connector-credentials-ui`, one `navigationContributions` row into `setup` / `group_integrations`, priority 120, one `component` item `nav_connector_credentials` with `componentRef: 'automation:connector-credentials'`, icon `key-round`, `requiredPermissions: ['manage_metadata']`), `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIALS_COMPONENT_REF` and `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIALS_NAV_CAPABILITY`. All three are additive constants; no existing export, route, key or shape changes. **Right**, and the shape is the one `MARKETPLACE_BROWSE_UI_BUNDLE` / `MARKETPLACE_INSTALLED_UI_BUNDLE` (`cloud-connection/src/marketplace-ui.ts`) and `CONNECT_AGENT_UI_BUNDLE` (`@objectstack/mcp`) already use, parsed under `ManifestSchema` by the new `connector-credentials-ui.test.ts`.
2. `AutomationServicePlugin` registers the bundle through the `manifest` service in a `kernel:ready` hook placed after the inert-mode return (`plugin.ts` L1764-1769, `registerConnectorCredentialsUi` L940-947, swallowing a missing manifest service). So a one-shot tool and a bare kernel register nothing, and the entry lives and dies with the automation service (cloud ADR-0009 shape, the triage's ⛔). **Right**; pinned by the `LiteKernel` boot (registered once), the inert boot and the no-manifest boot cases.
3. The capability gate is the door's own: `manage_metadata` is what every one of the three credential routes asks (#27237), so the entry is shown exactly to the viewers the routes admit. **Right.**
4. `@object-ui/app-shell` registers the component for `automation:connector-credentials` in `builtinComponents.tsx` (L153-166), eagerly like `automation:packaged`; the shell declares no entry and no route. `check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` gains the bundle as a contributor row (the `@objectstack/mcp` row's shape, since `kernel:ready` never fires in the census context), and the four platform locales label `nav_connector_credentials`. **Right** (`check:app-nav-i18n` 13 contributors, 58 ids, every id labelled, per the report).
5. `builtInLocales` (`ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/index.ts`) is annotated with `typeof` of each pack per key instead of inferred: the same type, emitted as references so the declaration stays serializable (TS7056) after the 43 new `connectorCredentials` keys. **Right**, no surface change.
6. No `packages/spec` edit, no governed path, no new route: the page and the step consume #27237's three routes as shipped. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/27238-connector-credentials-page.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, all **patch**. The additive barrel export on `@objectstack/service-automation` follows this package's own precedent (#28070, `RunIdentityContext` barrel-exported as patch with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`), and the `@object-ui/*` group's (#28151). The nav entry is a new contribution, not a change to one. `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` sit line-initial on the PR body and the changeset. **Consistent.**

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared.
- `Clause-②` measured `yes (widening)` by the dev against the claim's `no`; the seat amended the claim (6528022573) and routed the review here. Answered in ①.1.
- The step sits after the install, not before it (the ruling text says install-local "prompts for the missing refs of the package being installed"): the dev measured that the door answers `404` for a reference no installed package declares, so a pre-install value could not be stored; the step opens in the install result where the connectors already exist degraded. A faithful reading of the ruling's intent (the administrator supplies the credential during the install flow and may skip); noted for the seat's ACCEPT, not a contract matter.
- Cloud ask 6473504855 adopted: the step reads the same `credential-refs` route after any install landing in this runtime, so hosted installs get the prompt with no cloud change; the hosted install path itself stays cloud#3352's (triage 6522868103).
- `Skills-docs: updated here` as a paragraph pair in `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` instead of a new page (the card's `Skills-docs` named an administrator page): a prose face, the seat reads it in ACCEPT; the dedupe reasoning (the existing "Setting a credential" section) is sound.
- Three things only a live stack can show (the entry in a real Setup sidebar for admin vs member, a real install-local flipping a degraded connector, the walled posture sentence on a `group` deployment) were not run: see S1.
- Head moved from the report's `e7b058e5` to `32e531dd` by one docs commit (`marketplace-handbook.mdx`), prose only.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note.

Should-fix (none blocks the declaration):
- **S1** The card's acceptance bullets (install HotCRM through the Console with no env vars; the Slack ref missing → fill → ready without restart; skip at install) are live-stack scenarios that jsdom cannot show. The seat should run, or file as a QA probe, the install-local round trip on a dev stack before or right after landing, and record the result on the card.
- **S2** `priority: 120` places the entry after Connect an Agent (110) and before Cloud Connection (200) by reading the other contributors' constants; a one-line pin in `check-app-nav-i18n` (or the bundle test) asserting the group order would keep a later contributor from silently reordering it.
